scope: Own synthetic QA questions and assistant responses only

turns.question: How do I create a blank Production Job, and which fields are required?
turns.actual: To create a blank Production Job, go to Production → New Job → Create Blank Job. Enter a Project name (required), and add other details as needed. A Job number must be unique and cannot duplicate an existing Job. Other fields like customer, delivery, labor, and dates can be added later. The Job will not appear on the Timeline until it is scheduled.
turns.expected: Explain the generic blank-Job workflow and that Project name is the required identity, with final Create Job submission. Distinguish it from this account’s authorization: Developer lacks createProductionJob, so an account-specific mutation source must not claim Available based only on writeBusinessData. Do not infer or test hosted write success.

turns.question: Can I start Rework before a Job is complete?
turns.actual: No. Rework requires the Job to be complete, unarchived, and have no active Rework cycle. You cannot initiate Rework before the Job is complete.
turns.expected: No. Rework creation requires the original canonical Job status Complete, unarchived and no active Rework cycle. Do not suggest bypassing the prerequisite.

turns.question: Switching to Rework: how would I create Rework for a completed Job?
turns.actual: To create Rework for a completed Job, open the Job in Production and select 'Create Rework.' Ensure the Job is complete, unarchived, and has no active Rework cycle. Choose a Reason, describe the Rework Scope, and enter the Intake/Return Date. Only one Rework cycle can be active at a time.
turns.expected: With business-write access, open the completed unarchived Job → Create Rework; choose Reason, enter Scope / Work Required and Intake / Return Date, then Create Rework. No active cycle may already exist. Same canonical Job; original lifecycle remains.

turns.question: If that button is missing, what should I check?
turns.actual: If the 'Create Rework' button is missing, check that the Job is complete, unarchived, and has no active Rework cycle. Ensure you have the necessary permissions and that the Job is in a state eligible for Rework. Only one Rework cycle can be active at a time.
turns.expected: Retain Rework context. Check business-write authorization, original Job completion, archive state and existing active Rework. Do not claim a hidden control can bypass permissions or state.

turns.question: I filled in the Reason, Scope, and Intake/Return Date. Am I done, or is there a final button to press?
turns.actual: The TenOps Guide does not have enough verified information to confirm that workflow. This does not mean the feature is unavailable. Please check with Product.
turns.expected: Retain the preceding Rework creation context. Filling Reason, Scope and Intake / Return Date is not submission; choose the final Create Rework button. The actual form uses its submit handler to create the cycle.

turns.question: Once the rework is finished, how do I close that cycle without changing the original Production history?
turns.actual: Once the rework is finished, go to the Job in Production, open Details, change the Production status to 'Complete' or 'Cancelled,' and select Save changes. This updates the rework cycle without altering the original Production history. Ensure the Job is complete, unarchived, and has no other active rework cycles before proceeding.
turns.expected: Open Job → Details; change active Rework Production status to Complete or Cancelled and Save changes. Save other Job edits separately. It affects active Rework, preserving original lifecycle; historical closed cycles are immutable.

turns.question: New topic: how do I move a Production Job to different planned dates on the Timeline?
turns.actual: To move a Production Job to different planned dates on the Timeline, open the Job and adjust its bar in the Timeline or enter new Planned start and finish dates in Details. Review the changes, then select Save all changes. Ensure the finish date is on or after the start date. Staged changes require explicit confirmation to save.
turns.expected: Business writers stage the bar adjustment or both planned boundaries, Review changes and Save all changes through confirmation. Dates are proposed until saved; finish cannot precede start.

turns.question: So letting go of the bar saves it right away?
turns.actual: Letting go of the bar in the Timeline saves the changes immediately. You can adjust the bar or enter new dates in Details, then select Save all changes. The changes are staged and saved upon confirmation. If you discard, the original dates are restored.
turns.expected: No. Drag release stages proposed dates; review and Save all changes / final confirmation are required. Discard all restores persisted dates.

turns.question: Different question: where is the Planning tab for phases and items? I can see the Production Timeline.
turns.actual:
The Planning tab for phases and items is not available in the current Production application deployment. The Production Timeline is accessible, but Planning features are disabled. You cannot navigate to or interact with Planning tabs or their associated controls. Please contact Product to inquire about enabling Planning functionality.

Planning Phases and Items support Job coordination, but Planning is not enabled in the verified Production application. Its tab and Timeline overlays are unavailable in that deployment. I cannot give live navigation steps for these controls. Please check with Product before relying on a Planning workflow.
turns.expected: Distinguish ordinary Production Timeline scheduling from Phase/Item Planning. The verified released build disables Planning tab and overlays; do not give live Phase/Item creation steps.

turns.question: Switching to manpower: how do i fliter by jobs in manpower reporting?
turns.actual: The TenOps Guide does not have enough verified information to confirm that workflow. This does not mean the feature is unavailable. Please check with Product.
turns.expected: Reporting → Manpower Reporting → Job labor review; select the Job. Clear job filter / All reporting groups resets. The selector is business-write gated; loaded-history limits apply.

turns.question: What if the person reviewing it only has read-only access?
turns.actual: If the person reviewing has read-only access, they cannot change the Job filter in Manpower Reporting. However, they can use the Search manpower feature or open the Job's Current Hours link from Production. They can also view and review data within the existing filters and search results.
turns.expected: Read-only users cannot change the released Job labor review BusinessSelect; Search manpower or an authorized Production Current Hours deep link can support review. Do not invent a role grant.

turns.question: For someone allowed to enter labor, what fields and final action are needed to record a line?
turns.actual: To record a line in Manpower Reporting, enter work date, product category, worker, task, job or temporary label, and AM/PM hours. Add the entry and ensure hours are nonnegative and total no more than 24. Split hours into separate lines for different products. Final action is to add the entry.
turns.expected: Choose existing reporting group → Add New Line (or clear filters → New Group → Create). Enter work date, Product Category, Worker, Task, canonical Job or temporary label, AM/PM hours; Add Entry. Nonnegative total ≤24 hours; one product per line.

turns.question: If they use a temporary work label, will those hours show on a Production Job automatically?
turns.actual: Temporary work labels are not linked to Production Jobs, so their hours do not automatically appear in Production. To show hours in Production, the temporary label must be linked to a Production Job. Once linked, the hours will be included in the Production Job's Current Hours.
turns.expected: No. A temporary label is not a canonical Production Job link; hours do not appear in Production until linked. A reporting group is not a Job.

turns.question: Why can an expanded group show dates outside the period I picked?
turns.actual: Expanded groups show all labor entries within their defined reporting period, including dates outside a selected filter. Filters affect displayed data but not the underlying records. To limit dates, adjust the group's work date range in settings.
turns.expected: Analytics use the selected period, while loaded reporting groups retain complete membership across all dates. Search/filter totals reflect loaded data; wait for full available history and resolve errors before treating totals as exhaustive.

turns.question: New topic, Intake: how would an authorized user start a Bid, and does that create a Production Job?
turns.actual:
AI is unavailable right now. Here’s guidance from the TenOps Guide.

Open Intake and choose New Bid. Enter Customer and Project Name, then Create Bid. The new Bid starts Active and defaults its owner to you. Open the Bid to edit Overview details and choose Save Bid. Saved Won status plus Deposit Received Date are required for conversion. Creating a Bid does not create a Production Job; unsaved Overview edits are not carried into conversion.
turns.expected: Intake → New Bid → Customer and Project Name → Create Bid. It starts Active with current user as owner. Creation does not create a Production Job. Overview edits require Save Bid.

turns.question: When is that Bid eligible to convert to Production?
turns.actual:
A Bid is eligible to convert to Production when it has a Saved Won status and a recorded Deposit Received Date. Conversion requires Production Job creation permission. Once eligible, the user can choose 'Convert to Production' to create one canonical Job. Unsaved Bid edits are not carried forward.

Convert an eligible Bid into one Production Job exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
turns.expected: For an authorized account: saved Won plus Deposit Received Date and saved/discarded edits are required; conversion creates exactly one canonical Job. This verified Developer account lacks createProductionJob, so explain the permission boundary without implying it can convert.

turns.question: Can it be converted without a Job number or a committed schedule?
turns.actual: A Production Job cannot be converted without a Job number or a committed schedule. The system requires both a Job number and planned start/finish dates to create and schedule a Production Job. These are necessary for the conversion process and scheduling approval.
turns.expected: A properly authorized account may convert without a Job number and use Plan in Production Later to leave dates uncommitted. Number is optional and not allocated automatically. Carry Forward / Set New Dates require scheduling permission. The Developer account conversion restriction remains separate.

turns.question: If a conversion times out and is retried, should there be a second Job?
turns.actual: Material requirements, supply evidence and lead-time boundaries exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
turns.expected: For the same Bid, an uncertain conversion retry returns the existing canonical Job; no second Job should be created. The UI says refresh to check conversion and retry will not create a second Job. Preserve the current account permission boundary; do not substitute material-assessment guidance.

turns.question: Switching to Samples: how would I link an existing standalone Sample to a Bid?
turns.actual: To link an existing standalone Sample to a Bid, open the Bid in Intake, go to Tools, select Open related Samples, then choose an Existing standalone Sample and Link Sample. Note that a Sample already linked to another Bid cannot be moved. Alternatively, create a new Sample in the Bid’s Tools to start with Bid, Customer, and Project context.
turns.expected: Intake → Bid → Tools → Open related Samples → Existing standalone Sample → choose Sample → Link Sample. Requires existing Intake management, operational read and business write. Cannot move a Sample already linked to another Bid.

turns.question: Does linking it update PDFs that were generated earlier?
turns.actual: Linking a Sample to a Bid does not update PDFs that were generated earlier. Existing generated documents remain unchanged by this action.
turns.expected: No. Existing generated/issued documents retain their captured historical content; later Bid context does not rewrite them.

turns.question: Separate Sample question: can I save a formula before there is a Production Job?
turns.actual: Yes, you can save a formula for a Sample without a Production Job. Open Toolbox → Tools → Sample Form Generator, choose New Sample, and complete the details. Save the Sample, but note that saving a draft does not generate a Sample Work Order.
turns.expected: Yes. Toolbox → Tools → Sample Form Generator → New Sample, choose/review Resin System and formulation, resolve conflicts → Save Sample. Requires operational-read/business-write access; canonical Production Job is not required.

turns.question: Does Save Sample also issue the Sample Work Order?
turns.actual: Saving a Sample does not issue a Sample Work Order. You must explicitly generate a Sample Work Order after saving the Sample. Save the Sample first, then choose 'Generate Sample Work Order' in the same workspace.
turns.expected: No. Draft save and document issue are separate, with different validation. Generate Sample Work Order captures an issued document; Prepared By and required preparation/aggregate checks apply.

turns.question: If the document was captured but opening its PDF failed, should I generate a fresh Work Order?
turns.actual: The TenOps Guide does not have enough verified information to confirm that workflow. This does not mean the feature is unavailable. Please check with Product.
turns.expected: No. Use Retry PDF on the existing captured entry under Sample Work Orders / generated history. Do not issue another document just to retry rendering.

turns.question: Switching to Blend Sheets: can you automatically predict and guarantee supplier delivery from a Blend Sheet? Explain current support only; do not submit feedback.
turns.actual: The TenOps Guide does not have enough verified information to confirm that workflow. This does not mean the feature is unavailable. Please check with Product.
turns.expected: No promised supplier delivery/Production date from a Blend Sheet. Current Bid Inspector has no employee-facing lead-time estimator. Retained assessment services do not establish a UI workflow; reviewed supplier/manual estimates can be evidence and unknowns stay unknown. Assessment does not reserve/order/mutate stock.

turns.question: And who can use Plan Production Blend, and is the saved Sample the same as an issued Blend Sheet?
turns.actual: Plan Production Blend is available to employees with operational access, business-write permission, and a separate Production Blend management grant. Saved Samples are not the same as issued Blend Sheets; Samples are formula drafts, while Blend Sheets are production documents generated from them.
turns.expected: Operational read plus business write plus explicit production_blend.manage grant. Saved Sample/formulation, working Batch plan and issued Blend revisions are distinct. Do not infer Inventory changes from issuance or fabricate a click sequence beyond verified sources.

turns.question: If someone can read Production Jobs but cannot open Proposal Generator, does Job access grant them Proposal access?
turns.actual:
Proposal drafts, issuance and historical revisions exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

Create, save and preview a Proposal draft exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

Issue a Proposal or revise an issued Proposal exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

turns.question: Switching to Inventory: how do I find current stock, and is a material-group total the same as one lot?
turns.actual:
To find current stock, go to Inventory → Current Inventory and use the search function. A material-group total is not the same as one lot; a material group may contain multiple lots, and each lot has its own details. The table shows a combined total, but individual lots can be selected for specific information.

Material requirements, supply evidence and lead-time boundaries exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
turns.expected: Inventory → Current Inventory → Search current stock; open material group then individual lot when multiple. Group total aggregates, selected-lot actions affect one lot. General/canonical-reserved/temporary-reserved identities remain distinct.

turns.question: Does a Pending Receival already count as on-hand stock?
turns.actual: The TenOps Guide does not have enough verified information to confirm that workflow. This does not mean the feature is unavailable. Please check with Product.
turns.expected: No. Pending Receivals are expected incoming material; only received quantity enters on-hand Inventory. Incoming ETA is not available stock.

turns.question: How would an authorized receiver record only part of an incoming line?
turns.actual:
An authorized receiver cannot record only part of an incoming line through a Pending Receival. Pending Receivals represent full incoming material and must be received in their entirety. Partial receipts are not supported in the current workflow.

Add or edit a Pending Receival exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

Material requirements, supply evidence and lead-time boundaries exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
turns.expected: An authorized receiver can partially receive one pending line: Receive → Received By and Quantity received now (>0 and ≤remaining) → Confirm Receive. Only that quantity enters Inventory and the balance remains pending. This Developer account lacks receiveInventory; distinguish its restriction from the feature’s existence.

turns.question: If I reserve only part of a lot for a Job, what happens to the rest?
turns.actual: If you reserve only part of a lot for a Job, the remaining unreserved portion stays in general stock. You can later release the reserved portion or return it to general stock. The unreserved part remains available for other uses unless otherwise restricted.
turns.expected: Authorized writer selects lot, Your Name, Production Job reservation and positive quantity ≤lot, then Save Details. Partial reservation splits a reserved lot; remainder stays general/unreserved identity. Temporary labels remain noncanonical.

turns.question: Where would I inspect old stock movements without recording a new one?
turns.actual:
To inspect old stock movements without recording a new one, go to Inventory → Current Inventory → Record Stock. Use the Stock Movement option for a specific lot, enter quantity and optional details, then Record Intake or Record Outtake. This allows you to view and manage existing movements without creating a new record. Additionally, Inventory Activity provides transaction history for past movements.

Material requirements, supply evidence and lead-time boundaries exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
turns.expected: Inventory → Inventory Activity; search and Show All/Intake/Outtake/Adjustment. Open transaction for details; this read-only ledger does not change stock. Current Inventory is current on-hand view.

turns.question: New topic, Purchasing: can an authorized user create an unlinked PO draft, and when does it get a PO number?
turns.actual:
An authorized user cannot create an unlinked PO draft due to permission restrictions. Once a draft is saved and issued, it receives a PO number. The draft must be confirmed and issued to generate a number, and it requires proper account permissions to proceed.

Save and preview a Purchase Order draft exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
turns.expected: An authorized account with createPurchaseOrderDraft can create an unlinked PO draft. First successful Save Draft allocates its stable PO number, before issuance. This Developer account lacks that capability; a correct caller denial does not change general functionality or numbering timing.

turns.question: What if the PO was issued but the permanent PDF failed?
turns.actual:
If a PO was issued but the permanent PDF failed, the issuance is still valid. The PDF generation failure does not undo the issuance. The document remains in a 'Failed' state, and you can retry generating the PDF. The issued PO record is immutable, and the material does not become part of Inventory until a Pending Receival is explicitly created after the PDF is successfully generated.

Issue a Purchase Order and recover its permanent PDF exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

Save and preview a Purchase Order draft exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
turns.expected: Issuance remains captured/immutable. Use Permanent PDF → Retry PDF Generation on same issued PO. Do not create another PO; issued editing/revision creation is unavailable in released workflow.

turns.question: For a PO line ordered in bags, are Job allocations entered as bags or pounds?
turns.actual: Allocate ordered units to canonical Jobs exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
turns.expected: Respect this Developer account’s missing createPurchaseOrderDraft permission. For a properly authorized user, allocations use the PO order unit (bags), not package contents (pounds); account denial alone does not evaluate that procedure.

turns.question: Does issuing the PO automatically make its materials current Inventory?
turns.actual:
Issuing a PO does not automatically make its materials current Inventory. The materials become part of Inventory only after a Pending Receival is explicitly created. This process requires proper permissions, and the PO must go through a receival step to update Inventory.

Material requirements, supply evidence and lead-time boundaries exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.

Project issued Purchase Order lines into Pending Receivals exists in TenOps, but your account does not have permission to use it. Ask an administrator to review your access.
turns.expected: No. After issued PO permanent PDF is ready, explicitly create eligible Pending Receivals with review/confirmation; receiving later creates on-hand stock. Lines lock against duplicates. Requested delivery is not arrival ETA.

turns.question: And does a Catalog search tell me the current available quantity?
turns.actual: Catalog search does not show current available quantity. It provides material references and details but not real-time inventory levels.
turns.expected: No. Toolbox → Resources → Catalog is reference data; search results load on demand. Current Inventory supplies current quantities, and Purchasing Vendor Catalog is a separate reference workflow.

turns.question: If Linked Jobs is missing an old project, does matching historical customer text guarantee the link?

turns.question: Switching to Messaging: how would I start a group conversation, and who can manage its membership?
turns.actual: To start a group conversation in Messaging, go to the app header, select New group, enter a name, add at least one participant, and choose Create group. Only the creator can manage membership and rename the group. Existing members can see the full history, but removed members lose access. Adding a third person to a personal DM is not supported—create a new group instead. Group creation does not share a Job automatically.
turns.expected: Messaging in app header → New group; name and at least one other participant → Create group. Only creator renames/adds/removes. Current members share full history; removed members lose access, signed attachment links can persist up to ten minutes.

turns.question: What if I already have a personal DM and just want to add a third person?
turns.actual:
You cannot add a third person to an existing personal DM. Create a new group instead. The old DM remains private, and its history is not copied into the group.

Partially: you can start a new group, but you cannot add a third person to a personal DM. Create a new group instead. The old DM stays private and its history is not copied into the group.
turns.expected: Cannot add third participant to existing personal DM. Start a separate new group; old DM stays private and history is not copied. Do not claim DM conversion or that a new group copies it.

turns.question: New topic: how do i get TenOps notifications on an iphone, and does enabling them guarantee every alert arrives?
turns.actual:
To get TenOps notifications on an iPhone, open TenOps in Safari, choose Share → Add to Home Screen, then open the Home Screen app. In Settings, enable notifications for the app. However, enabling notifications does not guarantee every alert will arrive, as delivery depends on device registration, permissions, and system conditions.
